title: Fourier coefficient expansion
statement: For each natural number $n$ and each function $p$ from the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to $\\mathbb R$, evaluate on the binary cube the polynomial whose coefficient at a subset $T\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$ is half the difference between the indicator of $T=\\varnothing$ and $(-2)^{|T|}$ times the sum of the Fourier coefficients of $p$ over all subsets containing $T$. This evaluation equals the function on the binary cube given by $x\\mapsto (1-p(\\sigma(x)))/2$, where $\\sigma$ sends each binary coordinate to its corresponding sign.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
